Accountable obligation owner.value: Named AML/OFAC Officer signs every file/no-file decision on a suspicious activity report; deputised to the Compliance Manager only in writing for a stated absence

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda POCA s.46 disclosure duty and the Proceeds of Crime (AML/ATF) Regulations 2008 read together with the BMA Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020) 3LOD/governance sections; US arm verified against 31 CFR 1025.320 (SAR-IC) and the current FinCEN SAR Electronic Filing Requirements; texts re-read at each annual policy refresh and on any FIU/FinCEN advisory

In-scope processes.value: Covered-product suspicious activity lifecycle for permanent life, annuity and life-settlement business: monitoring alert or staff internal report to the MLRO, case triage, investigation, SAR review committee decision, regulator filing, continuing-activity review at 90/120 days

In-scope systems.value: Actimize AML case manager holds the alert-to-SAR case; filing is made in the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System and the Bermuda FIU goAML portal, with acknowledgements filed back to the case

Compliance procedure documented.value: Suspicious Activity Reporting Procedure FIN-AML-07 — internal report intake, 30-day US / 14-day Bermuda clock start rules, five-part narrative standard, committee decision record, filing steps by portal, no-tipping-off rules

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Board Risk Committee; reviewed annually and re-approved on any FinCEN advisory, FIU typology notice or BMA Code of Conduct amendment

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per case: FinCEN SAR due 30 calendar days from initial detection of facts (60 where no subject is identified); Bermuda FIU disclosure due within 14 days of the initial internal notification; continuing-activity SAR due every 120 days while conduct persists

Deadline reminders configured.value: Actimize case SLA timers alert the assigned AML Analyst at day 10, the AML Officer at day 20 and the Head of Compliance at day 25 of the 30-day clock; a separate day-7 alert runs the 14-day Bermuda disclosure

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: SAR copy, BSA Identifier, goAML reference, narrative drafts, committee minutes and all supporting transaction/policy documents retained 5 years from the filing date in the restricted SAR vault

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any SAR filed after day 30 (or day 14 in Bermuda), any un-actioned internal report, and any confidentiality breach is raised as a financial-crime compliance issue with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every late filing, every decision not to file that audit challenges, and the closure of each SAR-timeliness issue

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All Actimize AML cases and MLRO internal reports raised in the quarter across life, annuity and life-settlement books, plus every SAR filed to FinCEN and every goAML disclosure made in the same window

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on deadline: one SAR filed past day 30 (or a Bermuda disclosure past day 14) fails the test; no-file decisions fail at a re-performance disagreement rate above 5% of the sample; any tipping-off instance is an immediate fail escalated to the Board Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven per case, so the test runs quarterly over that quarter's full case population, with an annual roll-up feeding the independent AML programme test

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must hold SAR-vault read access but must not have investigated, drafted or approved any sampled case

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly SAR timeliness and quality workpaper (case population extract, sample list, re-performance notes, deadline recomputation, exception log) held in the restricted SAR folder of the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: SAR filing log with BSA Identifiers and goAML references, acknowledgement receipts, committee decision minutes and the quarterly workpaper, producible to a FinCEN/BMA examiner within 5 business days without leaving the SAR vault

Regulator response path.value: The AML/OFAC Officer is the single point of contact for FinCEN, the Bermuda FIU and the BMA; law-enforcement and 314(b) contacts route to Regulatory Counsel before any SAR content is confirmed or released

checklist.step: Take in the alert or internal report and open a case
actions: In Actimize open Alerts ▸ My Queue and work items in Detection Date order; also drain the MLRO mailbox where producers and Contact Center Agents send free-text internal reports.

Create a case and record the trigger type: monitoring scenario id (early surrender, rapid free-look cancellation, third-party premium, structured cash payments), staff internal report, negative news hit, or law-enforcement enquiry.

Stamp the Initial Detection Date field with the date the first fact indicating possible suspicion reached the company — this date, not the case-open date, starts the 30-day FinCEN clock and the 14-day Bermuda disclosure clock.
Attach the source artefact (alert payload, the reporter's email, the screening hit) and mark the case Restricted so it is invisible outside the financial-crime group.
Assign the case to a Financial Crime Investigator and notify the AML/OFAC Officer through the Actimize assignment notice.
checklist.done: an Actimize case exists with a trigger type, an evidenced Initial Detection Date, the source artefact attached and a named investigator.

checklist.step: Confirm the customer and product fall inside the covered-product perimeter
actions: Pull the policy record and read product code, contract type and cash-value features to confirm it is a permanent life policy, an annuity contract or a life-settlement interest — the covered products under 31 CFR 1025.320.
Record the writing entity and its jurisdiction so the case is routed to the FinCEN path, the Bermuda FIU path, or both.

Where the product is term life, group life without cash value or a health contract, record the out-of-scope basis with the product code cited and still refer the conduct to SIU where fraud is suspected.
Write the covered/not-covered conclusion and its basis into the case Scope tab before any investigation time is spent.
checklist.done: the case states covered or not covered with the product code and writing entity cited, and the filing jurisdiction is set.

checklist.step: Build the transaction and policy history behind the alert
actions: Extract 24 months of premium receipts, loans, partial withdrawals, full surrenders, free-look cancellations, beneficiary changes and ownership changes for the policy and every other policy held by the same owner.

Ask Billing Operations for the payment instrument detail on each receipt: payer name, bank, country, instrument type (wire, ACH, cheque, money order, card) and whether the payer differs from the policy owner.
Build a dated transaction table showing amount, date, instrument, counterparty and the resulting policy action, and total the suspicious amount and the date range.

Flag the specific typology the pattern fits — early surrender after single premium, overpayment and refund to a third party, structuring below reporting thresholds, unrelated third-party premium payer.
Attach the transaction table to the case as the SAR evidence base.
checklist.done: a dated transaction table with payer detail, a totalled suspicious amount, a date range and a named typology is attached to the case.

checklist.step: Re-screen every party and identify the subjects
actions: Run the policy owner, insured, beneficiaries, assignees, payers and the writing producer through the screening system against OFAC SDN/consolidated, UN, UK OFSI, EU and the Bermuda designated-persons lists, plus PEP and adverse media.

Resolve each hit as true match or false positive with the discriminating data point recorded (date of birth, national id, address), and escalate any true OFAC match to blocking/rejection the same day.
Obtain from the servicing team the identification documents on file for each subject: full legal name, address, date of birth, tax identification or national id number, and occupation.
Record each subject in the case Subjects tab with role (owner, beneficiary, payer, producer) so Part I of the SAR can be completed without further research.
checklist.done: every party is screened with hits dispositioned, and each subject carries a complete identity set tagged with its SAR role.

checklist.step: Gather context from the distribution and servicing side without tipping off
actions: Ask the Agency Relations Manager for the producer's account of how the business was written — source of the client, source of funds stated at application, and any unusual instructions.
Ask the servicing team for call recordings and correspondence around the flagged transactions and pull them from the document repository.

Frame every request as a routine quality review: never tell the producer, the customer or any servicing staff that a report may be filed, and record in the case that the no-tipping-off instruction was given.
Where the producer is himself a subject, route the enquiry to the Producer Compliance Manager instead and keep the producer out of the loop entirely.
Log each enquiry with date, recipient and the answer received.
checklist.done: context enquiries are logged with answers, and the case records that no subject or producer was told a report may be filed.

checklist.step: Reach the file / no-file decision at the SAR review committee
actions: Table the case pack (transaction table, screening results, subject identities, context enquiries) at the weekly SAR review committee with the Head of Compliance and the SIU Manager.

Apply the statutory test in writing: does the company know, suspect, or have reason to suspect the funds derive from illegal activity, are designed to evade reporting requirements, or have no apparent lawful purpose.
Record the decision as FILE or NO FILE with the reasoning, the deciding officer, the date and the dissent if any — a no-file decision needs the same depth of reasoning as a filing.
Where the decision is FILE, confirm which regulator paths apply (FinCEN SAR, Bermuda FIU goAML disclosure, or both) and restate the due dates against the Initial Detection Date.
Sign the decision record and attach the committee minute to the case.
checklist.done: a signed, dated committee decision with the statutory test applied, the filing paths named and the due dates restated sits in the case.

checklist.step: Draft the SAR narrative to the who-what-when-where-why-how standard
actions: Open the narrative template and write in plain chronological English: who the subjects are and their relationship to the policy, what the activity was, when it occurred, where it happened (branch, portal, wire corridor), why it is suspicious, and how it was conducted.
State the total suspicious amount, the activity date range and the policy/contract numbers in the first paragraph so a law-enforcement reader gets the summary immediately.
Name the typology and the monitoring scenario that surfaced it, and list any prior SAR BSA Identifiers on the same subjects.
Strip every reference to the SAR itself, to internal legal advice and to the reporting employee's identity from the narrative.
Have a second AML Analyst peer-read the draft for the 5W+H elements and factual agreement with the transaction table before submission.
checklist.done: a peer-reviewed narrative exists carrying subjects, amount, date range, policy numbers, typology and prior BSA Identifiers, with no self-referential SAR language.

checklist.step: File the FinCEN SAR in the BSA E-Filing System within 30 days
actions: Log in to the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System and open Reports ▸ New Report ▸ FinCEN SAR for the registered filing entity.

Complete Part I Subject Information for each subject (name, address, TIN, date of birth, identification document, role, relationship to the institution) and tick 'all critical subject information unavailable' only where it genuinely is.

Complete Part II Suspicious Activity Information: amount involved, date range from and to, and the characterisation checkboxes (structuring, money laundering, terrorist financing, insurance-specific: excessive insurance, early policy cancellation, suspicious sources of funds).
Complete Part III with the branch/location detail and Part IV with the filing institution's contact office, then paste the approved narrative into Part V.
Validate the form, sign and submit; the submission must land on or before day 30 from the Initial Detection Date (day 60 only where no subject can be identified, and record that basis).
checklist.done: the FinCEN SAR is submitted with Parts I–V complete on or before the 30-day deadline computed from the Initial Detection Date.

checklist.step: Make the Bermuda FIU disclosure in goAML within 14 days
actions: Log in to the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency goAML web portal with the reporting-entity account and open New Report ▸ Suspicious Activity Report.
Complete the reporting-entity block, the transaction block (each flagged transaction with date, amount, currency, instrument and both parties) and the subject blocks from the case Subjects tab.
Paste the same approved narrative into the Reason for Suspicion field and attach the transaction table and identification documents as report attachments.
Submit within 14 days of the initial internal notification to the MLRO, in line with the POCA s.46 disclosure duty and the Code of Conduct reporting expectations.
Where the conduct also engages a US covered product, confirm the parallel FinCEN filing is in flight so the two records carry consistent subjects and amounts.
checklist.done: the goAML disclosure is submitted inside 14 days of the internal notification with transactions, subjects, narrative and attachments complete.

checklist.step: Capture the acknowledgements and identifiers back into the case
actions: Retrieve the BSA E-Filing acknowledgement from the Track Status screen and copy the BSA Identifier onto the case header once the status shows Accepted.
Retrieve the goAML report reference number and submission receipt and record it alongside.
Where the acknowledgement returns a warning or rejection, correct and re-submit within 5 business days and record both the original and corrected submission dates.
Set the case status to Filed and record actual filing date, computed due date and days-to-file on the SAR filing log.
checklist.done: the case carries the BSA Identifier, the goAML reference, the acknowledgement receipts and a days-to-file figure on the filing log.

checklist.step: Lock the SAR record down and enforce confidentiality
actions: Move the filed SAR, narrative and supporting pack into the restricted SAR vault and restrict the access group to the financial-crime team, the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel.
Ask the Identity Access Manager to confirm the vault access list quarterly and to alert on any grant made outside the approved group.
Brief anyone who touched the case in writing that disclosing the existence of a SAR to the subject or any unauthorised person is a criminal offence, and record the acknowledgement.
Route any subpoena, customer subject-access request or producer question that could reveal the filing to Regulatory Counsel before any response is given.
checklist.done: the SAR pack is in the restricted vault with a reviewed access list and written confidentiality acknowledgements from everyone who handled the case.

checklist.step: Decide and execute the customer and producer treatment
actions: Set the post-filing treatment: retain with enhanced monitoring, restrict transactions, decline further business, or exit the relationship — and record the rationale.
Where exit is chosen, work the surrender or non-renewal through the servicing team on ordinary commercial grounds only, with no reference to the report.
Raise the customer risk rating in the customer record and set the enhanced review cycle so the file is re-examined at the next trigger.
Where the producer's conduct is implicated, refer to the Producer Compliance Manager for appointment review and to SIU for parallel fraud investigation.
checklist.done: a recorded treatment decision is executed, the customer risk rating is updated and any producer referral is logged.

checklist.step: Run the continuing-activity review and file the follow-up SAR
actions: Set an Actimize review task 90 days after the filing to re-examine account and policy activity for the same subjects.

Where suspicious conduct has continued, file a continuing-activity SAR no later than 120 calendar days after the date of the previously filed report, ticking the Continuing Activity Report box and citing the prior BSA Identifier in Part V.
Where the conduct has stopped, record the closure conclusion, the evidence reviewed and the reviewer on the case before releasing the review task.
Repeat the 90/120-day cycle for as long as the conduct persists rather than treating the first filing as the end of the matter.
checklist.done: each filed case has a 90-day review outcome recorded, and any continuing conduct produced a follow-up SAR inside 120 days citing the prior BSA Identifier.

checklist.step: Report SAR volumes and themes to governance
actions: Prepare a quarterly financial-crime report showing SARs filed by jurisdiction, typology and product, average days-to-file, late filings and open cases past day 20.
State volumes and themes only — never subject names or narrative content — so the report can circulate to the Board Risk Committee without breaching SAR confidentiality.
Publish the pack to the board portal for the Board Risk Committee and record the committee's questions and directions in the minute.
Feed recurring typologies back to the monitoring team as candidate scenario tuning and to the Learning Development Manager as training content.
checklist.done: the quarterly pack is tabled at the Board Risk Committee with volumes, days-to-file and themes, and no subject-identifying detail.

checklist.step: Retain the SAR record for five years and prove retrievability
actions: Apply the 5-year-from-filing-date retention label to the SAR copy, the BSA Identifier record, the goAML receipt, the narrative and every supporting document.
Confirm the record is indexed by BSA Identifier, policy number, subject name and filing date so an examiner request can be met without a manual trawl.
Run an annual retrieval test on 5 archived SARs and record the time taken to produce the full pack.
Block deletion of any record inside the retention window with a legal hold flag and report attempted deletions to the AML/OFAC Officer.
checklist.done: every filed SAR pack is labelled for 5-year retention, indexed on four fields, and proven retrievable by an annual retrieval test.

testing.step: Build the population of alerts, internal reports and filings for the quarter
actions: Extract from Actimize every case and alert with a status change in the quarter, with fields: case id, trigger type, Initial Detection Date, decision, decision date, filing date, BSA Identifier, goAML reference.
Extract separately the MLRO mailbox internal-report log and the SAR filing log, and add any internal report that never became an Actimize case.
Add the FinCEN BSA E-Filing Track Status export and the goAML submitted-reports list for the same period so filings made outside the case system cannot hide.
Record the extraction date, the filters used and the row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: one population file exists combining Actimize cases, MLRO internal reports and both regulator submission exports, with extraction parameters recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the regulator systems of record
actions: Match every SAR on the internal filing log to a BSA E-Filing acknowledgement with an Accepted status and a BSA Identifier.
Match every Bermuda case to a goAML report reference and confirm the count agrees to the goAML submitted-reports list.
Investigate both directions: a filing with no case, and a case marked Filed with no acknowledgement, are each reconciliation breaks.
Clear or list every break before sampling and have the AML/OFAC Officer initial the reconciliation.
testing.done: the internal filing log reconciles both ways to BSA E-Filing and goAML, with residual breaks listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of filed SARs and 100% of cases where days-to-file exceeded 25 days.
Take 25 no-file decisions at random using a seeded selection, plus every no-file case where the suspicious amount exceeded USD 250,000.
Record the seed, population size, stratum sizes and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Confirm coverage of every trigger type (monitoring scenario, staff internal report, screening hit, law-enforcement enquiry) and add rows where a type is unrepresented.
testing.done: the sample is drawn from a recorded seed, covers all filed SARs, all late-risk cases and every trigger type, and is re-drawable.

testing.step: Re-perform the file / no-file judgement independently
actions: Read the transaction table, screening results and context enquiries for each sampled case without first reading the committee decision.
Apply the statutory test yourself — knowledge, suspicion, or reason to suspect illegal source, evasion of reporting requirements, or no apparent lawful purpose — and write your own conclusion.
Compare to the recorded committee decision; disagreements and decisions with reasoning too thin to test are both exceptions.
For sampled no-file cases, confirm the reasoning addresses the specific typology flagged rather than restating that the customer is long-standing.
testing.done: each sampled case has an independent written conclusion compared to the committee decision, with disagreements listed.

testing.step: Trace each filed SAR to the regulator record and its identifiers
actions: In the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System open Track Status and search the recorded BSA Identifier for each sampled filing.
Confirm the filing entity, submission date and Accepted status, and that the report is a SAR and not a mistyped form.
Open the filed report and compare Part I subjects, the Part II amount and date range, and the Part V narrative to the case evidence.
Repeat in goAML for Bermuda-path cases, confirming the report reference, submission date and attachment count.
Capture the Track Status and goAML confirmation screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled filing is confirmed accepted in the regulator system with subjects, amount, date range and narrative agreeing to the case evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day and 14-day deadline maths
actions: For each sampled filing, re-derive the Initial Detection Date from the source artefact — the alert timestamp or the reporter's email date — rather than accepting the field value.
Recompute the FinCEN due date as Initial Detection Date + 30 calendar days (+60 only where no subject was identified and that basis is documented) and compare to the acknowledged submission date.
Recompute the Bermuda due date as internal notification date + 14 days and compare to the goAML submission date.
Recompute the continuing-activity due date as prior filing date + 120 days for every case with ongoing conduct.
List every filing past its recomputed due date with the number of days late.
testing.done: deadline maths is recomputed from source dates for every sampled filing and each overrun is quantified in days.

testing.step: Test narrative quality and subject completeness against the filing standard
actions: Score each sampled narrative against the 5W+H standard and fail any that omits the amount, the date range, the policy number or the mechanism of the activity.
Check Part I holds a complete identity set per subject, and that 'critical information unavailable' was ticked only where the case file genuinely lacks it.
Check the narrative carries no reference to the SAR itself, to legal advice or to the reporting employee.
Confirm prior BSA Identifiers on the same subjects were cited where earlier filings exist.
testing.done: each sampled narrative is scored against the 5W+H standard with subject completeness and prior-filing cross-references verified.

testing.step: Test confidentiality and vault access controls
actions: Pull the SAR vault access group membership and compare it to the approved financial-crime access list; every extra member is an exception.
Pull the vault read/download audit log for the quarter and test 15 access events back to a documented business reason.
Check the case record for each sampled filing holds a written no-tipping-off acknowledgement from everyone who handled it.
Test any customer complaint, subject-access request or subpoena touching a sampled subject for evidence that Regulatory Counsel cleared the response.
testing.done: vault membership matches the approved list, sampled access events are justified, and no tipping-off or uncleared disclosure is found.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception carrying case id, exception type (late filing, unactioned internal report, weak no-file rationale, narrative gap, access breach) and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — detection date mis-stamped, investigator capacity, unclear escalation path, scenario tuning gap — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days and, for any late filing, require a written explanation suitable for disclosure to FinCEN or the FIU on request.
Carry every open issue into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue with type, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the late-filing count, the no-file disagreement rate and the narrative pass rate and compare each to the stated thresholds (zero late filings; disagreement rate at or below 5%).
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting each element.
Have the reviewer, who investigated, drafted or approved none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper and confirm the segregation in writing.
Report the conclusion and any late filings to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the restricted SAR folder of the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with measured rates, a stated conclusion, evidenced reviewer independence and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: AML/OFAC Officer owns the annual AML, sanctions and cyber-conduct curriculum content and the completion outcome; delivery is run with the Learning Development Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the training pillar of the AML programme requirement at 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(3) covering employees and the insurance agents and brokers upon whom the insurer relies, read with Bermuda's Proceeds of Crime (AML/ATF) Regulations 2008 training duty and the BMA Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020) three-lines-of-defence and governance sections; re-verified at each annual curriculum refresh

In-scope processes.value: Annual AML/sanctions and cyber-conduct training cycle for covered employees (new business, underwriting, policy servicing, claims, finance, contact centre) and for every appointed producer and agency writing covered life, annuity and life-settlement products, including onboarding training inside 30 days of hire or appointment

In-scope systems.value: Cornerstone LMS holds curricula, assignments, assessment scores and completion certificates; the employee roster comes from Workday HCM and the producer roster from the agency/producer management system reconciled to NIPR appointments

Compliance procedure documented.value: AML & Sanctions Training Standard FIN-AML-11 — population definition rules, role-based curriculum matrix, 80% assessment pass mark, 30-day onboarding rule, escalation ladder for non-completion up to appointment termination

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the curriculum content approved annually by the AML/OFAC Officer and the training outcome reported to the Board Risk Committee

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle opens 1 March and closes 31 May with a hard completion date of 31 May; new hires and newly appointed producers must complete within 30 days of start or appointment date; the annual completion certification goes to the Board Risk Committee by 30 June

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS automated reminders at 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before the 31 May close, then daily overdue notices to the learner and their manager; producer reminders copy the Agency Relations Manager and escalate to appointment suspension at day 45 overdue

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Course content version, assignment list, completion date, assessment score and attestation text retained 5 years per learner per cycle in the LMS with an annual immutable export to the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every learner not complete at 31 May, every producer suspended for non-completion and every population-definition error is logged with root cause, owner and closure date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs the annual completion certification and approves every documented exemption or extension beyond the 31 May close

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All covered employees on the Workday HCM roster and all appointed producers on the agency/producer management system roster at the 31 May cycle close, plus every joiner and new appointment during the cycle year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% completion of covered employees by 31 May and at least 98% of appointed producers with every remaining producer suspended from writing new covered business; assessment pass mark 80%; any learner assigned the wrong role-based curriculum is an exception regardless of completion

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual, so the completion test runs once after the 31 May close, with a quarterly interim check on the 30-day onboarding rule for joiners and new appointments

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must sit outside Compliance and Learning & Development and must not have built, assigned or administered any tested curriculum

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual AML training completion workpaper (roster reconciliation, curriculum matrix mapping, completion extract, sample of certificates and scores, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under the cycle year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Course content packs by version, the role-based curriculum matrix, the per-learner completion register with dates and scores, and the signed board certification — producible to a FinCEN, BMA or state market conduct examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The AML/OFAC Officer answers training questions in an AML examination; producer-training questions in a state market conduct exam route through the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager with the same completion register

checklist.step: Define the covered population for the cycle
actions: Extract from Workday HCM every active employee with job family in new business, underwriting, policy servicing, claims, finance, contact centre, distribution, compliance, audit and technology, with employee id, manager, legal entity and hire date.

Extract from the agency/producer management system every producer and agency with an active appointment on a covered life, annuity or life-settlement product, with producer id, National Producer Number, appointing entity and appointment date.
Ask the Chief HR Officer's HR Operations team to confirm contractors and secondees with system access are included — access, not payroll status, decides coverage.
Record the population rule you applied and the extract date so the same rule can be re-run for the test.
checklist.done: a dated covered-population file exists for employees and producers with the inclusion rule written down.

checklist.step: Reconcile the producer roster to NIPR appointments
actions: Run the NIPR Gateway appointment report for each writing entity and state and download the active appointment list with National Producer Numbers.
Match the NIPR list to the internal producer roster on NPN and list producers appointed in NIPR but missing from the training roster, and vice versa.
Resolve each difference with the Agency Relations Manager: terminated appointments are removed, live appointments are added to the training population the same week.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the cycle folder — an incomplete roster is the most common cause of a failed training examination.
checklist.done: the training producer roster reconciles to NIPR active appointments by NPN with every difference resolved and signed.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum content against current typologies and regulatory change
actions: Review the last cycle's content against FinCEN advisories issued in the year, Bermuda FIU typology notices, OFAC programme changes and the BMA Code of Conduct governance and 3LOD expectations.
Add the year's real internal cases in anonymised form — early surrender after single premium, third-party premium payer, free-look abuse, sanctions near-match handling.

Set the required learning outcomes: recognise covered products, recognise red flags, know how and to whom to make an internal report, know the 14-day and 30-day reporting clocks, know that tipping off is an offence.
Hand the outline to the Instructional Designer with the assessment blueprint (minimum 15 questions, 80% pass mark, randomised bank).
checklist.done: the cycle content outline is approved with year-current advisories, anonymised internal cases and stated learning outcomes.

checklist.step: Build the role-based curriculum matrix
actions: Define curricula in the LMS: AML Core (all covered staff), AML Advanced (new business, underwriting, servicing, claims, finance), Sanctions Screening Operations (screening and payments staff), Producer AML (appointed producers), Board & Senior Management AML briefing.
Map each Workday job family and each producer appointment type to exactly one curriculum in the matrix and have the AML/OFAC Officer approve the mapping.
Set duration, sequencing and the assessment attached to each curriculum, with retakes capped at three attempts before manager escalation.
Version the matrix with the cycle year so an examiner can see who was required to take what.
checklist.done: every job family and appointment type maps to one approved curriculum in a versioned matrix.

checklist.step: Author and quality-check the course and assessment
actions: Build the SCORM package with scenario-based modules and knowledge checks that mirror the approved learning outcomes.
Write the assessment bank so every learning outcome is covered by at least two questions and set randomised delivery with an 80% pass mark.
Test the package on desktop and mobile, confirm completion and score write-back to the LMS transcript, and confirm accessibility (captions, screen-reader labels).
Have the AML/OFAC Officer sign off the final content and record the content version id that will appear on every completion certificate.
checklist.done: a signed-off, version-stamped SCORM package with a mapped assessment bank passes technical and accessibility checks.

checklist.step: Assign the training and open the cycle
actions: Load the employee and producer populations into the LMS as dynamic groups keyed to the Workday job family and the producer appointment feed so leavers and joiners flow automatically.
Assign the mapped curriculum to every learner with an assignment date of 1 March and a due date of 31 May.

Send the launch communication from the Head of Compliance stating the deadline, the 80% pass mark and the consequence of non-completion, and copy the Agency Relations Manager on the producer communication.
Confirm the assignment count reconciles to the covered-population file before announcing the cycle open.
checklist.done: every learner in the population file carries a due-dated assignment and the assignment count reconciles to the population.

checklist.step: Deliver the 30-day onboarding training for joiners and new appointments
actions: Configure the LMS rule that auto-assigns AML Core plus the role curriculum on the Workday hire event, due 30 days from start date.
Configure the equivalent rule on the producer appointment feed so a newly appointed producer is assigned Producer AML due 30 days from the appointment date.
Block system entitlements for new joiners in screening and payments roles until AML Core is complete by flagging the access request to the Access Management Analyst.
Report weekly on joiners and new appointments approaching day 25 to their manager and the Agency Relations Manager.
checklist.done: hire and appointment events auto-assign training due at day 30, with weekly at-risk reporting running.

checklist.step: Run the senior management and board briefing
actions: Schedule the annual AML and financial-crime briefing for the Board Risk Committee and the executive committee within the cycle window.
Cover the year's SAR volumes and themes, sanctions exposure, the three-lines-of-defence roles for cyber and financial crime, and the directors' own obligations.
Record attendance in the minute and load an attendance record for each attending director and executive into the LMS as a completion so the population has no gap at the top.
Publish the deck to the board portal and note any board direction for the following cycle.
checklist.done: the board and executive briefing is delivered, minuted, and recorded as LMS completions for every attendee.

checklist.step: Monitor completion and escalate slippage weekly
actions: Run the LMS completion report every Monday split by legal entity, department and producer agency, showing assigned, complete, in progress and not started.
Send each department head and each agency principal their own outstanding list rather than a company-wide percentage.
Escalate to the divisional executive at 30 days before close where completion is below 80%, and to the Head of Compliance at 14 days where it is below 95%.
Publish the weekly trend on the compliance dashboard so the Board Risk Committee sees the run-in to 31 May.
checklist.done: a weekly completion report is issued by department and agency with documented escalations at the 30-day and 14-day gates.

checklist.step: Handle assessment failures and repeat non-completers
actions: Pull the list of learners who failed the assessment twice and book them into a live remediation session covering the failed outcome areas.
Record the session date, attendee list and the retake result, and refer any third failure to the learner's manager and the AML/OFAC Officer.
Analyse the question-level failure data and hand items with a company-wide failure rate above 30% to the Instructional Designer as content defects, not learner defects.
Track each remediation case to a passed score before the cycle close.
checklist.done: every double failure has a recorded remediation session and a final outcome, and high-failure questions are referred as content defects.

checklist.step: Enforce the consequence for producers who do not complete
actions: At 31 May, list every appointed producer with no completion and send a final 14-day notice copying the agency principal.
At day 45 overdue, set the producer's status to suspended for new covered business in the producer management system so submissions are rejected at intake.
Where non-completion persists past 90 days, initiate appointment termination and process the state termination through NIPR Gateway with the correct reason code.
Record every suspension and termination with its date and basis in the producer file.
checklist.done: no producer writes new covered business after day 45 overdue, and every suspension or termination is dated and evidenced.

checklist.step: Close the cycle and export immutable evidence
actions: Freeze the cycle in the LMS at 31 May and export the completion register: learner id, name, role, curriculum, content version, assignment date, completion date, score and attempt count.
Export the course content packs by version and the curriculum matrix version alongside the register.
Load the export into the compliance evidence repository under the cycle year with a 5-year retention label and a read-only flag.
Confirm the register row count equals the covered population count plus in-cycle joiners, and explain any difference in the cycle note.
checklist.done: a frozen, read-only completion register with content and matrix versions is filed under a 5-year retention label and reconciles to the population.

checklist.step: Certify the cycle to governance
actions: Prepare the annual training certification by 30 June stating the covered population, completion percentages for employees and producers, exceptions and the consequence applied.
State explicitly that content covered the covered-product perimeter, red flags, internal reporting, the 14-day and 30-day reporting clocks and the tipping-off prohibition.
Sign the certification and table it at the Board Risk Committee, recording approval in the minute.
File the signed certification with the completion register so the two travel together in an examination.
checklist.done: a signed annual certification with population, completion rates and exceptions is approved and minuted by the Board Risk Committee by 30 June.

checklist.step: Feed training outcomes back into the financial-crime programme
actions: Compare the count and quality of staff internal reports to the MLRO before and after the cycle, by department.
Where a department that touches covered products filed no internal reports in the year, treat it as a training effectiveness gap and schedule a targeted session, not a repeat of the same e-learning.
Feed question-level failure themes and the internal-report pattern into next cycle's learning outcomes.
Record the effectiveness conclusion in the cycle note so the next cycle starts from evidence rather than from last year's deck.
checklist.done: a written effectiveness conclusion links internal-report behaviour and assessment data to next cycle's learning outcomes.

checklist.step: Retain training evidence and prove retrievability
actions: Apply the 5-year retention label to the completion register, content versions, curriculum matrix and certification for each cycle.
Index the register so a single learner's full training history can be produced by employee id or National Producer Number.
Run a retrieval test on 5 randomly chosen learners across two cycles and record the time taken to produce content version, completion date and score.
Prevent deletion inside the retention window and report attempted deletions to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: training evidence is retained 5 years, indexed by employee id and NPN, and proven retrievable by a documented test.

testing.step: Rebuild the covered population independently
actions: Pull your own Workday HCM active-employee extract as at 31 May with job family, hire date, manager and legal entity, and apply the documented inclusion rule yourself.
Pull your own producer extract from the agency/producer management system for active appointments on covered products with NPN and appointment date.
Compare your rebuilt population to the population file Compliance used and list every learner present in one and not the other.
Record extraction dates, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently rebuilt population exists and every difference against the Compliance file is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the producer population to NIPR
actions: Run the NIPR Gateway active-appointment report per writing entity and state as at 31 May and download the NPN list.
Match NPN by NPN to the training roster and quantify producers appointed in NIPR with no training assignment.
Test 10 producers the company removed from the roster back to a NIPR termination transaction with an effective date before 31 May.
Treat any appointed producer with no assignment as an exception irrespective of production volume.
testing.done: the producer population is reconciled to NIPR appointments with unassigned appointed producers quantified as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample across curricula and populations
actions: Take 40 employees stratified across AML Core, AML Advanced and Sanctions Screening Operations, and 40 producers across at least 10 agencies.
Take 100% of in-cycle joiners and newly appointed producers subject to the 30-day onboarding rule, up to 25 of each.
Take 100% of directors and executives subject to the board briefing.
Record the seed, strata and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible stratified sample covering all curricula, joiners, new appointments and the board is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the curriculum assignment judgement
actions: For each sampled learner, read the Workday job family or producer appointment type and determine from the approved matrix which curriculum should have been assigned, without first looking at the assignment.
Compare to the curriculum actually assigned in the LMS; a completion of the wrong curriculum is an exception even where the learner scored 100%.
Test the matrix itself for coverage: list any job family touching covered products that maps to no curriculum.
Confirm the matrix version tested is the one approved for the cycle by the AML/OFAC Officer.
testing.done: each sampled learner's assigned curriculum is independently re-derived from the approved matrix and differences are listed.

testing.step: Trace completions to the LMS transcript and certificate
actions: In Cornerstone open Reports ▸ Transcript for each sampled learner and read completion date, content version, assessment score and attempt count.
Confirm the score meets the 80% pass mark and the completion date falls on or before 31 May, or within 30 days of the hire or appointment date for onboarding rows.
Download the completion certificate and confirm it names the same content version the AML/OFAC Officer approved for the cycle.
Where the completion was loaded manually — for example board attendance — trace it to the signed attendance sheet or minute.
testing.done: every sampled completion traces to a transcript record with a passing score, an in-window date and the approved content version.

testing.step: Recompute completion rates and the 30-day onboarding maths
actions: Recompute employee completion as completions on or before 31 May divided by the independently rebuilt covered population, and compare to the 100% threshold.
Recompute producer completion the same way against the 98% threshold and identify the shortfall by agency.
For each joiner and new appointment, recompute due date as hire or appointment date + 30 days and compare to the completion date, listing days late.
Compare your recomputed rates to the rates in the signed board certification; any overstatement is a reportable exception.
testing.done: completion rates and onboarding day counts are recomputed from the rebuilt population and reconciled to the board certification.

testing.step: Test content sufficiency against the obligation
actions: Open the cycle content pack and evidence coverage of each required outcome: covered-product perimeter, red flags by product, the internal reporting route to the MLRO, the 14-day Bermuda and 30-day FinCEN clocks, the tipping-off prohibition and sanctions escalation.
Map at least two assessment questions to each outcome and flag any outcome with no question behind it.
Check the pack cites the year's FinCEN advisories and FIU typology notices rather than repeating the prior year's material.
Confirm the producer curriculum covers producer-specific red flags at point of sale, not just an abridged employee deck.
testing.done: every required learning outcome is evidenced in the content and backed by at least two assessment questions.

testing.step: Test that non-completion consequences were actually enforced
actions: List every producer incomplete at day 45 overdue and check the producer management system shows a suspension flag effective on or before that date.
Pull new-business submissions received after each suspension date for those producers; any accepted submission is a control failure, not a documentation gap.
Check every incomplete employee in a screening or payments role had the entitlement block applied by the Access Management Analyst.
Confirm every extension or exemption beyond 31 May carries a written Head of Compliance approval with a stated reason and a new date.
testing.done: suspensions, entitlement blocks and approved extensions are evidenced for every incomplete learner, with no post-suspension business accepted.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception carrying learner or agency identifier, exception type (missing from population, wrong curriculum, late completion, below pass mark, consequence not enforced) and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — roster feed gap, matrix mapping error, appointment feed latency, manager non-escalation — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 60 days and require completion of the correct curriculum before the issue can close.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue with type, root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare recomputed employee completion to 100%, producer completion to 98% and the onboarding late count to zero, and state each result.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references behind each element, including the content sufficiency assessment.
Have the reviewer, who neither built, assigned nor administered any tested curriculum, sign the workpaper and confirm the segregation in writing.
Report the conclusion to the Board Risk Committee alongside the Head of Compliance certification and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository under the cycle year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with measured completion rates, a content sufficiency view, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Chief Audit Executive owns the independent test of the AML programme as the third line of defence and reports the result directly to the Audit Committee, not through Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the independent testing pillar of the AML programme requirement at 31 CFR 1025.210(b)(3), read with the Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) s.5/s.6 compliance-function and internal-audit-function duties and the BMA Insurance Sector Operational Cyber Risk Management Code of Conduct (2020) three-lines-of-defence expectation; texts re-read when the audit scope is set each year

In-scope processes.value: The full AML/CFT and sanctions programme for covered life, annuity and life-settlement business: the written programme and its board approval, the AML/OFAC Officer's designation and standing, customer identification and beneficial-ownership collection, risk rating, monitoring scenarios and tuning, sanctions screening, SAR decisioning and filing, training, record retention, and the third-party reliance arrangements with producers

In-scope systems.value: AuditBoard carries the audit programme, testing steps, evidence and issue tracking; evidence is drawn from NICE Actimize (AML), the sanctions screening system, Cornerstone LMS and the policy administration system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Internal Audit AML Programme Audit Manual IA-AML-01 — annual risk assessment and scope setting, pillar-by-pillar test programme, sampling standards, evidence and workpaper standards, issue rating scale, Audit Committee reporting protocol

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee as part of the annual audit plan; scope changes mid-year require Audit Committee chair approval recorded in the minute

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual: audit plan approved by the Audit Committee in Q4 for the following year, fieldwork closes by 30 September, draft report to management for response within 15 business days, final report and opinion to the Audit Committee at its Q4 meeting, before the board's annual AML programme approval

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard milestone alerts at fieldwork start, at 30 and 10 days before the 30 September fieldwork close, at day 10 of the 15-day management response window, and 20 days before the Q4 Audit Committee paper deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Audit programme, workpapers, sample selections, evidence attachments, management responses and the final report retained 7 years from report issue in AuditBoard with an annual export to the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every audit finding is rated (high/medium/low), assigned to a named first- or second-line owner with an agreed action and due date, and re-tested at closure; overdue high findings are reported to the Audit Committee each meeting

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Audit Executive signs closure of every finding only after re-performance evidence is inspected; management self-attestation alone never closes a high-rated finding

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The AML programme's own control population for the audit year: new covered-product policies issued, monitoring alerts generated and dispositioned, sanctions screening hits cleared, SARs and goAML disclosures filed, training assignments and completions, and CIP/beneficial-ownership records collected

Pass/fail thresholds.value: A pillar fails where any control is absent, or where sample deviations exceed 5% for detective controls and zero for the SAR deadline and sanctions blocking controls; two or more failed pillars drives an ineffective overall opinion and a report to the BMA

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual independent testing; a full-scope audit runs each calendar year with interim continuous-monitoring analytics each quarter on SAR timeliness and screening backlog so the annual opinion is not the first sight of a problem

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Quality reviewer is an audit team member with no role in the fieldwork; where Internal Audit itself is assessed, an external firm performs the review and reports to the Audit Committee chair

Evidence location for test results.value: AuditBoard engagement file for the year holding the risk assessment, scope memo, per-pillar test programmes, sample listings, evidence attachments, findings and management responses, with the signed report exported to the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Scope memo, per-pillar test programmes with results, the finding register with remediation status, the signed report and opinion, and the Audit Committee minute recording receipt — producible to a FinCEN, BMA or state examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Audit Executive presents the audit result to the BMA or a FinCEN examiner directly; the Head of Compliance answers on remediation status, and Regulatory Counsel clears any disclosure of a failed pillar to a regulator before it is made

checklist.step: Set the annual scope from a documented AML risk assessment
actions: Read the enterprise AML/CFT risk assessment, the prior year's audit findings and their closure evidence, and any BMA or state examination findings issued since.

Score each programme pillar — written programme and board approval, designated officer, CIP and beneficial ownership, risk rating, monitoring, sanctions screening, SAR decisioning and filing, training, record retention, producer reliance — on inherent risk and control maturity.
Write the scope memo naming the pillars in scope, the entities and product lines covered, the audit period, and the pillars deliberately excluded with the rationale.
Table the scope memo with the annual audit plan for Audit Committee approval in Q4 and record the approval in the minute.
checklist.done: an Audit Committee-approved scope memo exists naming in-scope pillars, entities, period and stated exclusions.

checklist.step: Confirm auditor independence and competence before fieldwork
actions: Obtain a written independence declaration from every assigned auditor confirming no prior role in designing, operating or approving any AML control in the audit period.
Record each auditor's AML competence — qualification, prior AML audit experience, training completed in the year — in the engagement file.
Where no internal auditor is independent of a pillar (for example where Internal Audit helped remediate it), engage an external firm for that pillar and record the reason.
Confirm the reporting line runs to the Audit Committee and that neither the Head of Compliance nor the AML/OFAC Officer can alter the audit conclusion.
checklist.done: signed independence declarations and competence records exist for every auditor, with any independence gap covered by an external provider.

checklist.step: Test the written programme and its board approval
actions: Obtain the current written AML/CFT programme and compare its contents to the required pillars — internal policies and controls, designated compliance officer, ongoing training, independent testing, and risk-based customer due diligence including beneficial ownership.
Trace board approval to a dated board or Board Risk Committee minute on the board portal and confirm approval falls inside the last 12 months.
Compare the programme's stated scope to the covered-product perimeter and flag any covered product the programme does not address.
Check version control: the programme in the policy repository must be the version the board approved, not a later working draft.
checklist.done: the written programme covers every required pillar and the operative version traces to a board approval inside 12 months.

checklist.step: Test the designation and standing of the AML/OFAC Officer
actions: Trace the officer's appointment to a board resolution naming the individual and the role.
Read the job description and the reporting line and confirm direct access to the board or Board Risk Committee independent of the executive chain.
Test that the officer was given the resources claimed: headcount versus approved establishment, system access to Actimize and the screening system, and the training budget actually spent.
Interview the officer on escalations refused or overturned in the year and trace any instance to its record — an overturned SAR decision is a serious finding.
checklist.done: the officer's board appointment, independent reporting line and actual resourcing are evidenced, with any overridden decision investigated.

checklist.step: Test customer identification and beneficial-ownership collection
actions: Extract every covered-product policy issued in the audit period with owner type, issue date, premium and the producing agency.
Sample 60 policies stratified across product, channel and risk rating, over-weighting single-premium and third-party-payer cases.
For each, inspect the identification evidence on file: name, address, date of birth, tax or national identification number, document type and number, and the verification date relative to issue date.
For entity-owned policies, inspect the beneficial-ownership certification for each 25%-or-more owner and the control person, and confirm it was collected at or before issue.
List missing, expired or post-issue verifications as findings with the policy number and the gap in days.
checklist.done: 60 sampled policies are inspected for complete, timely CIP and beneficial-ownership evidence, with gaps quantified in days.

checklist.step: Test customer risk rating and enhanced due diligence
actions: Obtain the risk-rating methodology and the factor weights, and reproduce the rating for 30 sampled customers from the underlying data — geography, product, payment method, PEP status, source of funds.
Compare your reproduced rating to the system rating and investigate every difference, including ratings manually overridden downward.
For every high-risk customer in the sample, inspect the enhanced due diligence file: source of wealth evidence, senior approval and the date of the last periodic review.
Test that overdue periodic reviews are reported — a high-risk customer past review date with no escalation is a control failure.
checklist.done: 30 risk ratings are independently reproduced, differences investigated, and EDD files with senior approval evidenced for high-risk customers.

checklist.step: Test transaction monitoring coverage and scenario tuning
actions: Obtain the Actimize scenario inventory with thresholds, the coverage matrix mapping scenarios to the risk assessment's typologies, and the last tuning study.
Identify typologies in the risk assessment with no detection scenario behind them and raise the gap as a finding.
Reconcile the transaction feed into Actimize to the policy administration and billing source systems for one month, by record count and value, to prove no data is dropped before detection.
Read the tuning study for above-the-line and below-the-line testing evidence, and challenge any threshold raised without documented below-the-line results.
Test 25 dispositioned alerts for a documented rationale and for closure inside the SLA.
checklist.done: scenario coverage is mapped to typologies, the data feed reconciles for a test month, and tuning and alert disposition are evidenced.

checklist.step: Test sanctions screening operation and list currency
actions: Confirm which parties are screened — owner, insured, beneficiaries, payers, assignees, producers — and at which events (application, issue, servicing change, claim, payout, list update).
Check list update logs for OFAC, UN, OFSI, EU and Bermuda designations and quantify the lag between publication and load; anything beyond 24 hours is a finding.
Inject a controlled test record matching a known SDN entry into a non-production screening run and confirm it alerts at the configured fuzzy-match threshold.
Sample 25 cleared hits and re-perform the true-match/false-positive decision against the list entry, checking the discriminating data point was recorded.
Confirm any true match in the period was blocked or rejected and reported to OFAC within the required timeframe.
checklist.done: screening coverage, list currency, threshold effectiveness and 25 re-performed hit decisions are evidenced, with true matches traced to blocking and reporting.

checklist.step: Test SAR decisioning, filing timeliness and confidentiality
actions: Take the year's full SAR population and all no-file decisions above the escalation threshold from the Actimize case export.
Recompute days-to-file from the evidenced Initial Detection Date against the 30-day FinCEN and 14-day Bermuda deadlines, and list every overrun with its day count.
Re-perform 20 no-file decisions against the statutory suspicion test and challenge any rationale that relies on customer tenure rather than the flagged conduct.
Trace 15 filings to the BSA E-Filing acknowledgement and BSA Identifier and to the goAML report reference.
Test SAR vault access membership against the approved list and check for any tipping-off instance in case correspondence.
checklist.done: SAR timeliness is recomputed for the full population, 20 no-file decisions re-performed, 15 filings traced to acknowledgements and vault access tested.

checklist.step: Test training coverage and record retention
actions: Reconcile the LMS covered population to the Workday HCM roster and the producer roster and quantify anyone required but unassigned.
Sample 30 learners and inspect completion date, assessment score and the content version on the certificate against the approved cycle content.

Test the record retention control by requesting five specific records at random — a SAR pack, a CIP file, a screening hit disposition, a training record and a monitoring alert disposition — and time the retrieval.
Confirm each retrieved record is complete and inside its retention window (5 years for SAR and AML records) and that deletion is blocked.
checklist.done: training population and completions are tested, and five record types are retrieved intact within their retention windows with timings recorded.

checklist.step: Test the reliance placed on producers and third parties
actions: List the agencies and third parties the insurer relies on for customer identification or ongoing monitoring under the AML programme.

Open each agreement in the contract repository and confirm it contains the AML obligations: identification standards, record production on request, training, audit rights and prompt notification of suspicion.
Sample 10 agencies and obtain their annual AML certification and evidence the insurer actually exercised its audit or record-request right in the period.
Where reliance exists with no contractual clause or no exercised oversight, raise a finding against the Third-Party Risk Manager and the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every reliance relationship is traced to a contractual AML clause and to evidence of oversight actually exercised in the period.

checklist.step: Rate findings and agree remediation with named owners
actions: Rate each finding high, medium or low using the manual's criteria: regulatory breach or undetected exposure drives high, documentation-only drives low.
Issue the draft report to the Head of Compliance and the AML/OFAC Officer for management response within 15 business days.
Agree an action, a named owner and a due date for each finding, and reject responses that promise to 'monitor' rather than change a control.
Load each agreed action into AuditBoard with its due date, and escalate any finding management declines to accept to the Audit Committee chair as a risk-acceptance item.
checklist.done: every finding is rated, has a management response inside 15 business days, and carries an agreed action, owner and due date in AuditBoard.

checklist.step: Issue the report and opinion to the Audit Committee
actions: Write the report with scope, work performed by pillar, sample sizes, results, findings and an overall opinion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective.
State explicitly that the testing was independent, naming who performed it and the basis of their independence from the AML programme.
Publish the report to the board portal for the Q4 Audit Committee meeting, ahead of the board's annual approval of the AML programme, and present it in person.
Record the Audit Committee's receipt, questions and directions in the minute — an unread report does not satisfy the independent testing pillar.
checklist.done: a signed report with a stated overall opinion is tabled, presented and minuted at the Q4 Audit Committee before the board approves the programme.

checklist.step: Re-test and close findings on evidence
actions: At each finding's due date, request the remediation evidence — the changed procedure, the new scenario, the completed training, the backfilled CIP files.
Re-perform the control on a fresh sample rather than accepting the owner's attestation, and record the sample and result in AuditBoard.
Extend the due date only with written Audit Committee chair approval, and report every overdue high finding at each committee meeting until closed.
Close the finding only on the Chief Audit Executive's signature after the re-performance evidence is inspected.
checklist.done: each finding is closed only after a fresh-sample re-performance and a Chief Audit Executive signature, with overdue high findings reported each meeting.

checklist.step: Retain the engagement file for seven years
actions: Export the AuditBoard engagement file — scope memo, independence declarations, per-pillar programmes, sample listings, evidence, findings, responses and the signed report — at report issue.
Apply the 7-year-from-issue retention label and index the export by audit year, pillar and finding id.
Run an annual retrieval test on one prior-year engagement and record the time taken to produce the scope memo, a named sample listing and the signed report.
Block deletion inside the retention window and report attempted deletions to the Audit Committee chair.
checklist.done: the engagement file is exported, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by year and pillar, and proven retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of AML controls that should have been independently tested
actions: Extract the full AML/CFT and sanctions control inventory from the GRC platform with pillar, control owner, frequency and risk rating as at the audit year end.

Add the pillars named in the regulation — written programme, designated officer, training, independent testing, risk-based CDD including beneficial ownership — so an unregistered control cannot be missed.
Extract the AuditBoard scope memo and test programme list for the same year.
Record the extraction date and row counts and note any control added to the inventory after the scope memo was approved.
testing.done: a control population combining the GRC inventory and the regulation's named pillars sits alongside the audit's tested-control list.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit scope to the control population
actions: Match each control in the population to a test step in the AuditBoard programme by control id.
List every in-scope control with no test step, and every test step with no control behind it.
For each control excluded from scope, read the rationale in the scope memo and challenge exclusions that rest on 'tested last year' where the control changed in the period.
Have the Chief Audit Executive initial the reconciliation and the residual exclusion list.
testing.done: every AML control either maps to an audit test step or to a challenged, documented exclusion, with the reconciliation initialled.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of audit test steps to re-examine
actions: Take 100% of test steps covering the SAR deadline control, sanctions blocking and beneficial-ownership collection — the zero-tolerance controls.
Take 20 further test steps at random across the remaining pillars using a seeded selection.
Take 100% of steps that concluded 'no exceptions' on a sample of fewer than 15 items, where the conclusion may be thinly supported.
Record the seed, strata and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all zero-tolerance steps, 20 random steps and every thin-sample conclusion is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the auditor's judgement on the sampled steps
actions: Open each sampled step in AuditBoard, read the test objective and the evidence attached, and form your own conclusion before reading the auditor's.
Re-perform the underlying test on a fresh item — re-read a CIP file, re-decide a screening hit, recompute a days-to-file figure — rather than reviewing the workpaper alone.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one; a right conclusion reached on evidence that does not support it is still an exception.
Check the sample size on each step meets the manual's standard for the control's frequency and risk rating.
testing.done: each sampled step has an independent re-performance note and a sample-size adequacy check against the audit manual.

testing.step: Verify independence and competence claims behind the testing
actions: Read the independence declaration for every auditor who worked on the engagement and check the signature date pre-dates their first fieldwork entry in AuditBoard.
Cross-check each auditor's name against the AML control owner list, the SAR committee attendance list and the remediation action owner list — any overlap voids independence for that pillar.
Confirm the audit reporting line to the Audit Committee is recorded in the internal audit charter and that the charter is board-approved and current.
Where an external provider covered a pillar, confirm the engagement letter, its scope and its direct report to the Audit Committee chair.
testing.done: every auditor's independence is verified against control-owner, SAR-committee and remediation-owner lists, with the charter and any external engagement confirmed.

testing.step: Trace the report and opinion to the Audit Committee record
actions: Locate the signed report in the board portal pack for the Q4 Audit Committee meeting and confirm the version tabled matches the signed final.
Read the minute and confirm the committee received the report, discussed it, and recorded any direction — receipt alone is the minimum evidence of the pillar.
Confirm the tabling date pre-dates the board's annual approval of the AML programme so the board approved on an informed basis.
Confirm the report states an overall opinion in the manual's language rather than a narrative that avoids a conclusion.
testing.done: the signed report is traced to the Q4 committee pack and minute, tabled before board approval, and carries an explicit overall opinion.

testing.step: Recompute the annual frequency and coverage maths
actions: Compute the interval in months between the prior year's report issue date and this year's; anything beyond 12 months breaches the annual independent-testing expectation.
Compute pillar coverage as pillars tested divided by pillars in the regulation's list and state the percentage.
Recompute the deviation rate on each sampled test step and compare to the 5% detective-control threshold and the zero threshold for SAR deadline and sanctions blocking.
Compare your recomputed rates to those stated in the report and treat any understatement as a reportable exception.
testing.done: the testing interval, pillar coverage percentage and per-step deviation rates are recomputed and reconciled to the issued report.

testing.step: Test that findings were remediated on evidence, not attestation
actions: Extract every finding raised in the prior two audit years with its rating, owner, due date and closure date.
Sample 15 closed findings, weighted to high ratings, and inspect the closure evidence attached in AuditBoard.
Fail any high-rated closure supported only by a management statement with no fresh-sample re-performance behind it.
Recompute the overdue days on every open finding and check each overdue high finding appears in an Audit Committee minute.
testing.done: 15 sampled closures are inspected for re-performance evidence and every overdue high finding is traced to a committee minute.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception carrying the pillar, exception type (control untested, independence impaired, thin sample, unsupported closure, report not tabled) and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — scope memo gap, auditor capacity, evidence standard not applied, committee calendar slip — and a named owner, which for audit-side exceptions is the Chief Audit Executive.
Set a remediation date inside 90 days and require the untested pillar to be covered by an out-of-cycle test rather than deferred to next year.
Carry every open issue into next year's scope memo as a mandatory coverage item.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue with pillar, root cause, owner, remediation date and a mandatory next-year coverage commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compare pillar coverage, the testing interval and deviation rates to the stated thresholds and record whether any pillar failed and whether two or more failed.
Write the conclusion — the independent testing obligation is met, met with exceptions, or not met — with workpaper references behind each element.
Have the reviewer, who performed no part of the AML audit fieldwork and owns no AML control, sign the workpaper and record the basis of that segregation.

Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and, where the obligation is not met, notify the BMA through Regulatory Counsel; file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the audit year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states pillar coverage, the testing interval, deviation rates and an explicit conclusion, with committee reporting and any regulator notification recorded.
